predecessors.note: Cliopatria splits one line of shahs into a 'Khwarezmid Dynasty' row (1094-1201) and this 'Khwarezmid Empire' row (1202-1235); the two Wikipedia articles are 'Anushtegin dynasty' and 'Khwarazmian Empire'. capitals.name: Gurganj (Urgench)
capitals.note: Infobox: Gurganj (1077-1212). The page's text on Muhammad II says he left 'Gurganj and the main court to be governed by his mother' in 1218.

capitals.name: Samarkand
capitals.note: Infobox: Samarkand (1212-1220); the Muhammad II page says he 'moved the capital to Samarkand' in 1218. Samarkand surrendered to the Mongols on 17 March 1220.

capitals.name: Ghazni
capitals.note: Infobox: Ghazni (1220-1221), the seat of Jalal ad-Din before the Indus.

capitals.name: Tabriz
capitals.note: Infobox: Tabriz (1225-1231); Jalal ad-Din set himself up there on 25 July 1225. 1222-1224 is a gap: he was in India and returned to Persia in late 1223.

rulers.name: Ala ad-Din Muhammad II
rulers.title: Shah
rulers.note: 'was the Shah of the Khwarazmian Empire from 3 August 1200 to December 1220'; he died on the Caspian island of Ashur-Ada. His father Tekish ruled 1172-1200 (Khwarazmian Empire page).

rulers.name: Jalal ad-Din Mingburnu
rulers.title: Shah
rulers.note: 'ruled the remnants of the Khwarazmian Empire and northwestern India from 1220 to 1231'; killed on 15 August 1231.

keyframe_review.note: 1.80 M km2 for 1202-1205; the page's infobox has only 2.3 M km2 for 1210 and 3.6 M km2 for 1218, so this earlier shape cannot be compared. Contents: Khwarazm, 1,660 of the 2,206 cells of Khorasan (Merv taken in September 1201, Muhammad II page), Kerman, and Persian Iraq to Hamadan and Isfahan, which the page dates to Tekish ('In 1194, Tekish defeated the Seljuq sultan of Hamadan, Toghrul III'; 'the Caliph accepted him as the sultan of Iran, Khorasan, and Turkestan in 1198'). The same page says Muhammad II took 'all of Persian Iraq' only by late 1217, so Hamadan and Isfahan may be drawn too early for 1204-1216; no page opened covers 1200-1217 there. fx-27: Lorestan (121 cells) subtracted. The Khorshidi page has Shoja al-Din Khorshid 'independent ruler of Lur-e-Kuchak' from 1184 (died about 1224) and never names the Khwarazm Shahs; the Khwarazmian pages date only Persian Iraq (Hamadan, Isfahan, Rayy), Kerman, Azerbaijan and Fars (via Ghiyath, 1224), not Lorestan. Fars stays in the shapes: the Salghurids page has Sa'd I (r. 1198-1226) 'acknowledging the Khwarazm Shahs as his overlord', and data/hierarchy.csv draws the Salghurids inside Khwarazm. fx-37: the Bakhtiari country and Idaj (98 cells, the Hazaraspid core) subtracted. The Khwarazmian Empire page never names them (it gives Persian Iraq, Arran, Azerbaijan and Derbent by late 1217) and the Hazaraspids page has Malik Hazarasp (r. 1204-1248) as an independent ruler at Idaj who 'assisted Jalal-al-din Khwarezmshah' against the Mongols, an ally; Khuzestan and Kohgiluyeh are not touched (the Hazaraspids reach them only in 1274, after this state ends).

region.text: Khwarazm, Khorasan and western Iran under Muhammad II, from Gurganj ; without the Hazaraspid core (Bakhtiari country and Idaj)

ledger.note: 1202: the shahs of Khwarazm hold an empire from the Aral Sea to Iraq. Muhammad II 'captured Merv in September 1201' (his page); Tekish had been accepted 'as the sultan of Iran, Khorasan, and Turkestan in 1198'; infobox 'Empire (1170s-1221)'. Cliopatria's row begins here as the successor of its Khwarezmid Dynasty row. fx-37: the Bakhtiari country and Idaj (98 cells) are subtracted: the Khwarazmian Empire page gives Persian Iraq, Arran, Azerbaijan and Derbent (late 1217), not the Hazaraspid country, and the Hazaraspids page has Malik Hazarasp (r. 1204-1248) an independent ruler at Idaj who 'assisted Jalal-al-din Khwarezmshah in his struggle against the Mongols' (an ally, undated).

region.text: Herat and Ghur, the Ghurid heartland

ledger.note: 1204: Muhammad II besieges Herat. The Ghurids 'laid siege to the city from March to the 2 May, 1204, inflicting serious losses'; he was defeated at Andkhud the same year (Ghurid dossier).

region.text: Herat and the Ghurid heartland of Ghur

ledger.note: 1206: Herat submits. It 'submitted to Muhammad after reports from Ghiyath arrived ordering him to submit', soon after Muizz al-Din's assassination (13 March 1206); Balkh held out for forty days that summer and Termez surrendered in late 1206.

1207: the Burhanids of Bukhara become vassals. Muhammad II marched in 'spring 1207, making the Burhanids his vassals'; the Karakhanid governor of Samarkand 'followed the Burhanids in submitting to Muhammad'.
1208: Herat falls. Muhammad II took Herat 'in July 1208 and executing Khwaja'; the Ghurids were reduced to vassals about 1209.

region.text: the Ghurid lands, Ghur, Firuzkuh and Ghazni

ledger.note: c. 1209: the Ghurids become Khwarazmian vassals. After Ghiyath al-Din Mahmud and Ali Shah were executed, 'all Ghurid territory becoming vassals of Khwarazm'; the page gives no year for the sentence.

1209: the Qara Khitai hold Samarkand. 'Samarkand was then occupied by the Qara Khitai, until Muhammad arrived and forced them to withdraw'; Muhammad had been 'defeated and captured by the Qara Khitai' in 1207.

ledger.counterpart: Mazandaran's local rulers (not named on the page)
ledger.note: 1210: Mazandaran is annexed. The page: 'resulting in Mazandaran's annexation into Khwarazm in 1210'; it does not name the previous rulers.
1210: the Qara Khitai are defeated. 'In the Ilamish Steppe in September 1210, where the Qara Khitai were utterly defeated.'

1212: Bukhara and Samarkand pass from vassalage to direct rule. The page: 'Almost all of Transoxiana ... were annexed by 1211-1212' and in 1212 'Muhammad attacked Samarkand ... executing' Sultan Uthman; it does not say when the Burhanids lost their vassal status (he 'marched on Bukhara in 1209'). Bridged.

region.text: Transoxiana with Sighnaq, Otrar and Uzkend on the Syr Darya

ledger.note: 1212: Transoxiana is annexed. 'Almost all of Transoxiana including cities like Sighnaq, Otrar and Uzkend were annexed by 1211-1212'; in 1212 he stormed Samarkand and executed Sultan Uthman. Muhammad took the title 'Second Alexander'.
1212: the court moves to Samarkand. Infobox: Gurganj (1077-1212), Samarkand (1212-1220); the Muhammad II page says he 'moved the capital to Samarkand' in 1218 (a disagreement between the two pages).

region.text: Fergana and the Kara-Khanid capitals of Uzgen and Samarkand

ledger.note: 1213: the Western Kara-Khanid Khanate is extinguished. Muhammad II ended it 'in 1213' and minted coins in Uzgen and Samarkand from 1213; Fergana was taken around 1213 'from the last Karakhanid garrisons there' (Muhammad II page).

region.text: the Ghurid lands, Ghur, Firuzkuh and Ghazni

ledger.note: 1215: the Ghurids are swept aside. Muhammad 'sweeping aside the Ghurids in 1215'; in November-December 1215 he captured Bamyan and Firuzkuh, and in 1216-17 he 'attacked Ghazni and crushed the Ghurid garrison there' (Muhammad II page).

region.text: Firuzkuh and Ghur, Bamyan and Ghazni

ledger.note: 1215-1217: Bamyan, Firuzkuh and Ghazni are annexed. 'In November-December 1215, Muhammad went to Afghanistan where he captured Bamyan, Firuzkuh'; in 1216-1217 'Muhammad attacked Ghazni and crushed the Ghurid garrison there'.

region.text: Rayy, Hamadan and Isfahan, all of Persian Iraq

ledger.counterpart: Persian Iraq's local rulers (not named on the page)
ledger.note: 1217: all Persian Iraq. Muhammad II 'captured Rayy with an enormous army of 100,000' and took 'Hamadan and Isfahan with minimal resistance': 'by late 1217, he controlled all of Persian Iraq'.

1217: Arran, Azerbaijan and Derbent become vassals. 'By late 1217 ... with Arran, Azerbaijan, and Derbent being his vassals'; he defeated the Eldiguzids, 'taking both Nusrat and vizier Rabib as prisoner'.

1219: Genghis Khan invades. 'Genghis Khan started his offensive on the town of Otrar where the incident had occurred in September 1219' (Muhammad II page); the Mongol page gives 'Between 1219 and 1221'. Jand fell on 21 April 1219.
1220: the court flees. Muhammad II reached Nishapur on 18 April 1220 and died on the Caspian island of Ashur-Ada in December 1220; Ghazni becomes Jalal ad-Din's seat (infobox: Ghazni 1220-1221).

1220: Bukhara and Samarkand fall. Bukhara was besieged on 7 February and surrendered on 10 February 1220; 'Genghis headed to the Khwarazmian capital of Samarkand and arrived in March 1220' (it surrendered on 17 March, Muhammad II page).

1221: Gurganj falls. The Mongol page does not date it ('Upon its surrender the Mongols broke the dams and flooded the city'); the Muhammad II page says only that 'Gurganj fell but street fighting persisted for several days' after seven months. The year is bridged from the page's 'Between 1219 and 1221'.

1221: Merv and Balkh fall. The Mongols 'arrived at Merv' after a night ambush on 24 February; 'After capturing Balkh in early 1221'; Tolui arrived at Nishapur on 7 April 'and the city captured the next day'.

ledger.counterpart: Lahore and the Punjab's rulers (not named on the page)
ledger.note: 1221-1223: Jalal ad-Din in the Punjab. After the Indus in November 1221 he 'crossed the Indus and settled in India', 'taking large parts of Lahore and the Punjab'; he returned to Persia 'in late 1223' at his brother's behest.

1221: the Mongols win the war for the empire. They sent 'a large army under Ögedei back to Ghazni' and Genghis 'defeated Jalal al-Din on the Indus River' (November 1221; Jalal page: 'crushed them in the ensuing battle in November 1221', i.e. after winning at Parwan in September).
1223: the Punjab is given up. He 'returned to Persia at the behest of his brother Ghiyath al-Din Pirshah', 'in late 1223'.

ledger.counterpart: Burak Hajib of Kerman (Qara Khitai of Kerman)
ledger.note: 1224: Kerman confirmed under Burak Hajib. 'In 1224, he confirmed Burak Hadjib, ruler of the Qara Khitai, in Kerman'; his brother Ghiyath submitted Hamadan, Isfahan and Fars the same year.
1225: Azerbaijan is annexed. The page says Jalal ad-Din 'captured Azerbaijan in 1225'; the 1217 vassalage becomes direct rule.
1225: Tabriz becomes the seat. Infobox: 'Tabriz (1225-1231)', 'Rump state (1225-1231)'.
1225: Tabriz. Jalal ad-Din 'set himself up in their capital of Tabriz on 25 July 1225', taking Azerbaijan from the Eldiguzids (Khwarazmian Empire page: 'captured Azerbaijan in 1225').

1226: Akhlat taken. Jalal ad-Din 'captured the town of Akhlat in Turkey from the Ayyubids' (1226); 'moved against Ahlat again in 1229', so it was not held. He also 'attacked Georgia and sacked Tbilisi' in 1226 (a raid, not a gain).

region.text: the rump state in western Iran, Northern Iran occupied by the Mongols

ledger.note: 1230: the Seljuks and the Mongols close in. 'Sultan Kayqubad I defeated him at Arzinjan ... at the Battle of Yassicemen in 1230'; Ögedei sent Chormagan with 30,000-50,000 men and the army 'occupied Northern Iran'.

region.text: the rump state in western Iran

ledger.note: 1231: the Mongols end the contest by killing Jalal ad-Din (15 August 1231); Chormagan's army had 'occupied Northern Iran'.

region.text: the rump state in western Iran

ledger.note: 1231: Jalal ad-Din is killed and the Khwarazmian rump ends. He 'was killed in 15 August 1231' (by a Kurd, in the Silvan mountains); 'A Khwarazmian rump state survived in western Iran until 1231' (Khwarazmian Empire page).

wars.name: Khwarazmian-Ghurid war
wars.outcome: Siege of Herat 1204; Herat taken July 1208; Ghurid lands vassals c. 1209; Muhammad II 'sweeping aside the Ghurids in 1215', Bamyan and Firuzkuh in November-December 1215, Ghazni in 1216-17.

wars.name: Khwarazmian conquest of Transoxiana and war with the Qara Khitai
wars.outcome: The Burhanids of Bukhara became vassals in 1207; the Qara Khitai were beaten in the Ilamish Steppe in September 1210; Transoxiana annexed by 1211-12; the Western Kara-Khanids extinguished in 1213.

wars.name: Khwarazmian conquest of Persian Iraq and march on Baghdad
wars.outcome: By late 1217 all of Persian Iraq was his and Arran, Azerbaijan and Derbent were vassals; the march on Baghdad stopped at the Asadabad Pass in a snowstorm; in February 1218 he removed the caliph's name from the khutba at Merv.
wars.note: The page does not date the march on Baghdad exactly.

wars.name: Mongol invasion of the Khwarazmian Empire
wars.outcome: Otrar (September 1219), Bukhara (February 1220), Samarkand (March 1220), Merv (February 1221), Balkh (early 1221), Nishapur (8 April 1221), Parwan (September 1221, a Khwarazmian win) and the Indus (November 1221, a defeat) destroyed the empire.
wars.note: The Mongol page dates the invasion only 'Between 1219 and 1221'.

wars.name: Jalal ad-Din's wars: Georgia, the Ayyubids and Rum
wars.outcome: Tbilisi sacked in 1226 (battle of Garni); Akhlat taken 1226 and attacked again 1229; beaten by Kayqubad I at Yassicemen in 1230; Chormagan occupied Northern Iran; Jalal ad-Din killed 15 August 1231.

certainty.note: No survey lines: the Syr Darya, Oxus and Indus frontiers, the vassal rims (Ghur, Arran, Azerbaijan) and the 1221-1231 itinerant state are approximate.

notes:
Cliopatria rows to correct: (1) the row runs to 1235 but the page ends the state in 1231; (2) the 1216 shape holds 1,815 cells in Pakistan (about 0.5 M km2) that no page opened supports; without them its area matches the infobox's 3.6 M km2 for 1218; (3) the 1220 shape keeps Khorasan and Khwarazm until 1226, but the Mongols held them from February-April 1221; (4) the 1227 shape keeps 428 cells of Iranian Khorasan. New keyframes 1221 and 1224 describe the post-Mongol state.
Not settled: whether Cliopatria's 'Khwarezmid Dynasty' (1094-1201, khwarezmid-dynasty, another part of this group) and this row are one state: same line of shahs, different Wikidata (Q486918 and Q63134381); the dossiers list each other as predecessor and successor and a reviewer may merge them. The status of Persian Iraq between 1200 and 1217 (Hamadan and Isfahan are in the 1202 shape although the page puts their capture in 1217); Kerman (inside the 1202 shape, 'seized by Oghuz Turks' in 1214-15); the date Gurganj fell (confidence 1); who held Lahore and the Punjab in 1221-23; whether Akhlat was held after 1226; the capital's years (infobox 1212 for Samarkand, Muhammad II page 1218; 1222-24 has none). The Khwarazmian hire by the Ayyubids and the sack of Jerusalem on 11 July 1244 (Khwarazmian Empire page) belong to the Khwarazmian remnants after the state's end and are not coded here.
Counterparts that need dossiers: the Burhanids of Bukhara, the Western Kara-Khanid Khanate (kara-khanid-khanate), the Eldiguzids (eldiguzids; me-09-x), the Qutlughkhanids/Qara Khitai of Kerman.
Page budget: four pages (budget five); the Ghurid and Qara Khitai articles were not opened because the Muhammad II page covers the campaigns.
